item.title: The Safer Affordable Fuel-Efficient (SAFE) Vehicles Rule III for Model Years 2022 to 2031 Passenger Cars and Light Trucks — Federal Register — Documents Matching 'Maine'
item.description: NHTSA, on behalf of the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT), is substantially recalibrating the Corporate Average Fuel Economy (CAFE) program to bring the program into compliance with the law and to remove previous regulatory distortions which have induced manufacturers to make design decisions that have neither aligned with market demand and the needs of American families nor have delivered the consistent improvements in the fuel economy performance of manufacturer fleets, as Congress intended. This recalibration finalizes amendments to fuel economy standards for light-duty vehicles for model years 2022- 2026 and MYs 2027-2031. This final rule also finalizes amendments to compliance aspects of the program, including to vehicle classification and other compliance pathways.

item.title: US Department of Labor awards $43 million to 7 states to support skills training in shipbuilding, manufacturing, aerospace, other critical industries — U.S. Department of Labor — News Releases
item.description: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor today announced the award of $43 million in Industry-Driven Skills Training Fund grants to seven states to invest in employer-driven skills training programs for critical industries like shipbuilding, advanced manufacturing, and nuclear energy.Administered by the department’s Employment and Training Administration, the second round of Industry-Driven Skills Training Fund grants will provide funding to State Workforce Agencies to provide outcome-based reimbursements to employers who provide training that is responsive to rapidly evolving skill requirements and local workforce needs. More than $10 million of the awarded funding supports occupations in the domestic shipbuilding industry and the maritime supply chain.“President Trump is restoring American manufacturing dominance, especially in critical industries like manufacturing, shipbuilding, and nuclear energy," said Acting Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling. "As we continue to see growth in the construction and manufacturing sectors these grants ensure that American workers have the skills necessary to fill the high-skilled and high-paying jobs that are driving our nation into a new era of industrial might and provide the economic security that previous administrations let slip overseas.”In September 2025, the department awarded more than $86 million to 14 states in the first round of Industry-Driven Skills Training Fund grants. Across both rounds, the grants invest more than $129 million in 21 states nationwide, including over $30 million for the shipbuilding industry. These investments support the Administration’s reindustrialization agenda and its commitment to building the skilled workforce for high-growth and emerging industries including advanced manufacturing; aerospace; infrastructure; building and construction; cybersecurity; domestic mineral production; healthcare; information technology; maritime supply chain; nuclear energy; quantum computing; and shipbuilding

item.title: US Labor Department obtains court order naming independent fiduciary for 401(k) plan of defunct WA-based aerospace company — U.S. Department of Labor — News Releases
item.description: SEATTLE – The U.S. Department of Labor has secured a court order to appoint an independent fiduciary to manage the abandoned 401(k) plan of a defunct Arlington-based aerospace company.The order, entered in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Washington, appoints AMI Benefit Plan Administrators Inc. as the independent fiduciary for the Commercial Aircraft Interiors LLC 401(k) Plan, which has been frozen since the employer shut down operations in 2023. In this role, the independent fiduciary will be able to distribute its assets to eligible former employees who have not been able to access their retirement savings because the only responsive company representative, Charles Pratt, lacked the legal authority needed to approve distributions. The independent fiduciary will also be able to formally terminate the plan.“The appointment of an independent fiduciary will give the participants in the Commercial Aircraft Interiors plan access to the funds that rightly belong to them,” said Liam Roberts, district director for the department’s Employee Benefits Security Administration in Seattle. “We urge all workers to contact the department for assistance when their retirement plan has been abandoned and they have not received the benefits to which they are entitled.”Under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act, all employee benefit plans are required to be managed by named fiduciaries. Without one, participants and beneficiaries cannot get information about their accounts or collect retirement benefits. WHEREAS, October 2026 marks the 81st anniversary of National Disability Employment Awareness Month; and

WHEREAS, workplaces across our state that are welcoming of the talents of all people, including people with disabilities, are critical to healthy communities and a strong economy; and

WHEREAS, while the employment rate of people with disabilities ages 16 to 64 in Maine has increased to 44 percent, it remains significantly lower than the 83 percent employment rate for Maine people without disabilities; and

WHEREAS, it is important that the State of Maine prepare all youth, including those with disabilities, for meaningful careers and an adulthood that includes employment; and

WHEREAS, Maine is an Employment First state, affirming employment as the first and preferred option for people with disabilities who receive services from state agencies; and

WHEREAS, people with disabilities, including people who are Deaf, Hard of Hearing, Late Deafened, Blind or with Low Vision make significant contributions to Maine's economy and communities; and

WHEREAS, activities during this month will reinforce the value and talent people with disabilities add to our workplaces and communities and affirm Maine's commitment to increasing access to good jobs and competitive, integrated employment for all workers, including those with disabilities;

NOW, THEREFORE, be it resolved that I, Janet T. Mills, Governor of the State of Maine, do hereby proclaim October 2026 as 

Disability Employment Awareness Month

throughout the State of Maine, and I call upon employers, schools, higher education institutions and other community organizations in Maine to observe October with appropriate programs and activities that celebrate the contributions of people with disabilities and promote access to good, in-demand jobs and career pathways such as registered apprenticeships for all Maine people.

In testimony whereof, I have caused

the Great Seal of the State to be

hereunto affixed GIVEN under my

hand at Augusta this twenty eighth day of

September Two Thousand Twenty-Six

WHEREAS, physician associates/assistants (PAs) are nationally certified and state-licensed medical professionals who diagnose illnesses, develop and manage treatment plans, prescribe medications, and often serve as a patient's principal healthcare provider; and

RULE 4A. PROBABLE CAUSE DETERMINATION UPON WARRANTLESS ARREST FOR ANY CRIME

Maine Forest Service report highlights effectiveness of forestry practices that protect water quality

October 1, 2026

AUGUSTA, Maine, October 1, 2026 - A new Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry Maine Forest Service (MFS) report underscores the effectiveness of environmentally friendly practices during timber harvesting. Released Oct. 1, the "Maine Forestry Best Management Practices Use and Effectiveness Data Summary" draws on hundreds of observations at timber harvesting sites across Maine.

This MFS study shows how forestry and timber industry professionals use recommended practices statewide. It also demonstrates that the risk to waterbodies greatly increases when they are improperly applied.

These measures, called Best Management Practices (BMP), are voluntarily implemented by professionals to help protect water quality in Maine's streams, rivers, lakes, and wetlands. They cover planning and application recommendations for activities such as stream crossings, road construction, and controlling erosion and sediment, the primary pollutants associated with timber harvesting.

Maines forest industry has made great strides in protecting water resources in recent decades, said State Forester and MFS Director Patty Cormier. The improvements weve identified through our BMP monitoring program are a testament to the ongoing value of the training that loggers, foresters, and woodland owners have participated in and applied. We thank them, our training partners, and collaborators for their contributions to this progress.

The report, released every two years, is the result of this monitoring from 2024 to 2025. It includes data from 165 timber harvesting sites and observations on over 700 individual activities, including around stream crossings, contaminants, and log landing placement.

This year's key findings include:

  • 74% of study sites applied appropriate practices on stream crossings. In many cases, they included planning to avoid crossings altogether. MFS emphasizes avoiding stream crossings when possible because they present the highest risk for sedimentation.
  • Soil movement monitoring found that, in 85% of cases, no sediment entered a water body. Of the 15% instances where sediment was recorded, 9% were in measurable amounts (~1 cubic foot or more of sediment), and 6% were trace amounts.
  • 87% of sites showed no evidence of chemical spills, a 10% decrease from the previous report. Reported spills ranged from minor drips to less than 10 square feet.
  • Progress on improving fish passage continues. Although the number of stream-crossing structures adequately spanning stream channels on haul roads decreased by 5% since the previous report, adequate crossings on operation trails increased by 17%.

This year's results are largely consistent with previous reports and continue to show that Maine's forestry and logging communities are using BMPs effectively. BMP use and effectiveness at timber harvesting operations are monitored regularly by the MFS District Foresters and Water Resources Specialist. In addition, MFS staff provide regular training and support for their application, with presentations and workshops across the state.

Since 2000, MFS staff have conducted a systematic statewide monitoring program of BMPs on a sample of timber harvesting operations across the state. Support from Maine landowners, loggers, and foresters has been critical to its implementation and effectiveness. MFS efforts also include financial incentives for loggers and foresters to acquire temporary bridges, which are among the most effective measures to install stream crossings with minimal impact.

In the latest report, and throughout the programs history, monitoring shows that when sedimentation was observed, it was most often due to inadequate BMP application. The risk of detrimental impacts also greatly increases if they are not applied or applied incorrectly. Previous reports and numerous national studies have also documented that BMPs help protect water resources when properly applied. The latest findings reinforce that continued monitoring, education, and training are key to sustaining the success of forestry BMPs and their environmental benefits.

The report can be found on the MFS Forest Policy and Management Division website.

item.title: General Provisions; Revised List of Birds Protected by the Migratory Bird Treaty Act — Federal Register — Documents Matching 'Maine'
item.description: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to revise the List of Birds Protected by the Migratory Bird Treaty Act (MBTA) by both adding and removing species and changing names to conform to accepted use by the scientific community. Reasons for the proposed changes to the list include adding species based on new taxonomy and new evidence of natural occurrence in the United States or U.S. territories, removing species no longer known to occur within the United States or U.S. territories, and changing names to reflect currently accepted taxonomy and nomenclature. The net increase of 25 species (32 added and 7 removed) would bring the total number of species protected by the MBTA to 1,131. We also propose to revise the names of species subject to specific migratory bird permit regulations to reflect currently accepted taxonomy and nomenclature. We are taking this proposed action because an accurate and up-to-date list of species protected by the MBTA is essential for public notification, regulatory, and law-enforcement purposes, and to ensure consistency in the use of common and scientific names across Service regulations.

item.title: US Department of Labor awards $10.2 million to 67 organizations to promote workplace safety and health training — U.S. Department of Labor — News Releases
item.description: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration today announced the award approximately $10.2 million in grant funds to 67 organizations across the nation to support education and training focused on worker safety to help employees and employers recognize serious workplace hazards and employ safety and health programs.Funded through the Susan Harwood Training Grant Program, the grants aim to advance worker safety and health by providing instructor-led training opportunities for workers and employers in small businesses with an emphasis on industries with high injury, illness, and fatality rates.The grants will fund training and education on hazard awareness, prevention, and controls to protect workers from on-the-job hazards through the development of quality classroom-ready training and educational materials that identify and prevent workplace hazards.The grants honor the legacy and work of Dr. Susan Harwood who, during her 17 years with OSHA, developed workplace safety guidelines for benzene, formaldehyde, bloodborne pathogens and lead in the construction industry. Harwood was also primary author of OSHA’s cotton dust standard which virtually eliminated byssinosis – a lung disease that causes asthma-like symptoms – among textile workers.Learn more about the Susan Harwood Training Grant Program and 2026 awardees.

item.title: US Labor Department finds railroad illegally terminated employee who refused to work during severe weather — U.S. Department of Labor — News Releases
item.description: LITTLE ROCK, AR – A U.S. Department of Labor Occupational Safety and Health Administration whistleblower investigation has concluded that Union Pacific Railroad Co. violated the Federal Railroad Safety Act when it removed from service and later terminated a North Little Rock yardman who notified management of nearby lightning and federal safety standards. OSHA determined that the employee voiced concerns about nearby lightning, cited OSHA and NOAA lightening safety guidelines, initiated a safety stand-down, and refused to work until the storm passed. Within minutes of the stand-down, Union Pacific removed the employee from service and was later charged with insubordination. Union Pacific terminated his employment on May 30, 2024.On June 10, 2026, OSHA ordered Union Pacific to remove from the employee’s employment records any reference of the incident, and pay back wages, lost benefits, compensatory and punitive damages totaling at least $304,869, and attorney’s fees. Union Pacific filed objections to OSHA’s order and has requested a hearing before a U.S. Department of Labor Administrative Law Judge.OSHA’s Whistleblower Protection Program enforces 25 whistleblower statutes that protect employees from retaliation for reporting violations of workplace airline, anti-money laundering, commercial motor carrier, consumer product, criminal antitrust, environmental, financial reform, food safety, health insurance reform, maritime, motor vehicle safety, nuclear, pipeline, public transportation agency, railroad, safety and health, securities, and tax laws.Editor’s note: The U.S. Department of Labor does not release the names of employees involved in whistleblower complaints.

item.title: Maine State Archives offers expanded digital access with Open Access — Maine Secretary of State — Bureau of Corporations, Elections & Commissions News
item.description: AUGUSTA, MAINE – Secretary of State Shenna Bellows today announced the official launch of Open Access, the Maine State Archives (MSA) new online platform for publicly accessible, digitized and born-digital public records. The platform can be accessed at https://digitalarchives.maine.gov or from the Maine State Archives section of the Secretary of State website. Open Access is the public-facing side of a strategic effort to maintain a digital preservation system for records of Maine state government. The system ensures the long-term preservation and accessibility of state records that are archival or subject to long-term retention. “From the beginning, I have been committed to improving efficiency and modernizing our systems to benefit Mainers and streamline access,” said Secretary Bellows . “Open Access will provide improved government transparency in a user-friendly platform that will be continuously expanded as more and more collections are imaged.” Overall, MSA’s collections span five centuries from the 1639 royal land grant to Sir Ferdinand Gorges to the 2024 papers of the Lewiston Tragedy Commission. One section of the site is devoted to Maine history before statehood, highlighting important records such as Revolutionary War land grants and the Rolls and Rosters Book of Orders for the 8th Division of the Maine Militia. The records of Maine’s involvement in the Civil War are extensive. Open Access currently holds just over 100,000 imaged records so far. “With more than 8 miles of documents in the Archives care, there is a long way to go to digitize them all, but it’s a great start,” said Maine State Archivist Christian Cotz. “We’re excited to continue to add records to the platform and provide Mainers from students to researchers with even more to discover each time they visit the site.” ###

Maine Paid Family and Medical Leave Program Publishes Actuarial Report, First Claims Report

October 1, 2026

For Immediate Release: Oct. 1, 2026

Media Contact: Autumn Mahoney, Communications Specialist media.dol@maine.gov

Actuarial report projects PFML Trust Fund will remain stable for the next 10 years

AUGUSTA - The Maine Paid Family and Medical Leave (PFML) program has published its second annual actuarial report, as well as its first claims report on Oct. 1, 2026.

PFML became law in 2023 and is a statewide program that provides eligible workers with up to 12 weeks of paid leave for medical, parental, family care, military family or safe leave.

The PFML program began accepting claims on March 30, 2026, and began paying benefits on May 1, 2026. This initial claims report covers the program's first three months of claims activity, from March 30 through June 30, 2026. Future claims reports will be published annually and will cover a full year of claims activity.

Highlights of the reports include:

  • The PFML Trust Fund remains solvent and based on updated revenue and claim expenditure, is projected to remain stable for the next 10 years.
  • The program received 8,376 applications between March 30 and June 30, 2026.
  • Among the claims approved, medical leave was the most common reason, followed by welcoming a new child and caring for a family member. Other leave reasons represented a very small portion of the overall claim volume.

"We are excited to see the PFML Program effectively off the ground and helping Maine workers and businesses through life's big moments, both now and for years to come," said PFML Director Luke Monahan.

More information on the PFML program, including how to apply, can be found on the program's website: https://www.maine.gov/paidleave/

Employees, employers and self-employed individuals with questions can call 207-621-5024 between8 a.m. and 5 p.m. Monday through Friday. Employees can send a message through the Benefits Application Portal, while employers and self-employed individuals can send a message through the Maine Paid Leave Contributions Portal.

October 1, 2026

For Immediate Release: Oct. 1, 2026

Media Contact: Autumn Mahoney, Communications Specialist media.dol@maine.gov

AUGUSTA - Gov. Janet T. Mills has proclaimed October 2026 as National Disability Employment Awareness Month (NDEAM).

October 2026 marks the 81st anniversary of NDEAM. Gov. Mills' proclamation recognizes the contributions of people with disabilities to Maine's workplaces, communities and economy and calls on employers, schools, higher education institutions and community organizations to promote access to good, in-demand jobs and career pathways, including registered apprenticeship.

"At a time when employers are searching for workers, talented Maine people with disabilities are ready and willing to participate in the workforce," said Jennifer Kimble, the chair of Maine's Commission on Disability and Employment. "Expanding recruitment and retention strategies that recognize the value of including workers with disabilities as benefits businesses, communities, and the individuals whose talents are too often underutilized."

The Commission on Disability and Employment was established by the legislature in 1997 and promotes collaboration with the public and private sectors to increase awareness and influence policy related to employment for people with disabilities. Its members envision a Maine workforce that includes all people with disabilities employed in jobs that meet both their economic and personal needs.

"National Disability Employment Awareness Month is an opportunity to recognize the skills, talents and contributions of Mainers with disabilities and to continue working toward workplaces where everyone has the opportunity to contribute and succeed," said Maine Department of Labor Commissioner Laura Fortman. "Maine's workforce needs every person who wants to work, and the Department of Labor and our partners are committed to helping people with disabilities pursue meaningful careers while helping employers connect with talented workers."

NDEAM has been observed nationally since 1945. The observance recognizes the contributions of people with disabilities and promotes employment opportunities and career pathways.

Yes, I was one of the lucky ones.

Many others who experienced domestic abuse are not so lucky. So to make sure that Maine people who have experienced or who are experiencing domestic abuse know that they're not alone and know that escape from violence is possible, I have declared October Domestic Violence Awareness Month in Maine.

Nationwide, one in four women and one in seven men has experienced abuse and violence by an intimate partner in their lifetime. MaineCare Telehealth Services Provider Licensure Requirements

Oct 05, 2026

As a reminder, all providers delivering telehealth services to MaineCare members must be enrolled with MaineCare and must comply with MaineCare Benefits Manual (MBM) Chapter I, Section 4: Telehealth Services.  

Chapter I, Section 4 requires that providers be “appropriately licensed, accredited, certified, and/or registered in the state where the member is located during the provision of the telehealth service.”  

This means that all providers delivering in-person or telehealth services to MaineCare members, who are in Maine at the time of the service, must hold appropriate Maine credentials or Interstate Licensure Compacts recognized by the Department of Professional and Financial Regulation (DPFR) or other appropriate organization.   

Pursuant to MBM, Ch. I, Section 1.18 failure to comply with these requirements can result in the denial of claims or recoupment of payment because services delivered without proper state licensure are not eligible for reimbursement. 

For questions, please contact your Provider Relations Specialist.

Oct 05, 2026

Reminds Maine people and visitors ticks remain active even as temperatures fall

As days get shorter and leaves begin to change, ticks remain active across Maine. The Maine Department of Health and Human Services’ Center for Disease Control and Prevention (Maine CDC) urges all Maine people and visitors to protect themselves from tick bites this fall.

Ticks can be active throughout the fall and during winter days, whenever temperatures rise above freezing. Fall is a busy time for outdoor activities, bringing people into contact with ticks more often. People may encounter them during everyday fall activities, like cleaning the yard or hunting.

Current year preliminary counts from the Maine Tracking Network show that health care providers reported over 5,000 cases of tickborne disease so far this year. This includes diseases like Lyme disease, anaplasmosis, and babesiosis.

“Many people think ticks are only a summer problem, but ticks can remain active throughout the fall,” said Maine CDC Director Puthiery Va. “You can enjoy Maine’s beautiful fall weather and outdoor activities while staying safe by taking a few simple steps before, during, and after can help protect you from tickborne disease.”

Ticks often live in wooded and brushy areas and areas with leaf litter. The Maine CDC encourages everyone to think TICKS when spending time outdoors: 

  • T – Take an EPA-approved repellent and use it before going outside. Use DEET, picaridin, IR3535, or oil of lemon eucalyptus on skin. Pre-treat clothing with permethrin.
  • I – Inspect your body daily. Check yourself, children, and pets for ticks after spending time outdoors.
  • C – Cover your skin. Wear long-sleeved shirts and long pants and tuck pants into socks. Light-colored clothing makes ticks easier to spot.
  • K – Know your surroundings. Be aware when you are in tick habitat and take extra precautions.
  • S – Shower after being outdoors. Showering helps wash off ticks before they attach. Put clothes in the dryer on high heat for at least 15 minutes before washing to kill ticks.

Remember to check for ticks after any outdoor activity and before bed each night. Check in areas where ticks may be easy to miss, including the scalp, behind the ears, under the arms, around the waist, between the legs, and behind the knees.

The most common symptoms of tickborne disease include flu-like symptoms. People who have Lyme disease may also find an expanding rash somewhere on their body. This rash can sometimes, though not always, look like a bullseye. If you experience any of these symptoms, talk to a health care provider and be sure to mention any recent tick exposure.

The University of Maine Cooperative Extension Tick Lab offers tick identification for free and tick testing to Maine residents for a $20 fee. Testing can take up to three days and should be used for surveillance purposes only, not for diagnosis. Finding a tick on you, even if it was attached, does not necessarily mean that it spread any germs to you. Find more information at ticks.umaine.edu. 

To learn more about how to stay tick free, visit the Maine CDC's website.

AUGUSTA, MAINE – Secretary of State Shenna Bellows today traveled to Brunswick Town Hall to mark the start of in-person, no-excuse absentee voting in Maine today. 

“Maine is always a national leader in voter turnout, and we saw record turnout in the June primary. In person absentee voting – Maine’s version of early voting – is part of the special sauce that makes voting convenient to the citizenry and drives up turnout,” said Secretary Bellows. “Anyone can vote early for any reason starting today until October 29, and there are lots of ways to vote absentee – in person, by mail or utilizing a secure ballot drop box.”

This week, voters who are not able to make it to the polls on Election Day or who simply wish to avoid the crowds can begin casting absentee ballots, either in-person at their local town hall or by mailing back their signed and sealed ballot or dropping it in a local secure ballot box. As of Friday, October 2, more than 70,000 Mainers had requested an absentee ballot. Absentee ballot reports are posted on Tuesdays and Thursdays on the Secretary of State’s website.  

Brunswick Town Clerk Fran Smith joined Secretary Bellows to talk about the tasks and challenges that face local election officials this election cycle and why Mainers can expect business as usual for the November 3 General Election.

“This is a busy but exciting time for our office, as I know it is for towns across the state,” said Brunswick Town Clerk Fran Smith. “Our local staff, as well as volunteers on Election Day, are so incredibly vital to ensuring everything runs smoothly right up through the counting of the ballots after the polls close on Election Day.”

As absentee voting gets underway, Secretary Bellows urged voters to make a plan to ensure their ballots are returned by close of polls on Election Day. In Maine, only those ballots received by close of polls are counted, regardless of postmark. Maine offers an online absentee ballot tracking service for voters to track the status of their absentee ballot to be sure that the clerk has received and accepted the ballot. If a voter’s ballot has not been received by Election Day, voters may go in person to the polls on November 3 to request that the missing absentee ballot be rejected or cancelled and cast a vote in person.

“The election should be business as usual this year because the election laws haven’t changed, but sometimes life gets in the way. We have all unfortunately experienced frustration with the postal service and things from everyday mail to prescriptions not arriving in a timely manner,” Secretary Bellows said. “That’s why it can be so helpful to vote early.”

“It’s exciting – Election Day will be here before we know it, and now is the time to make your voting plan,” she said.

New MaineCare Partner Portal: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Requirements

Oct 06, 2026

As a reminder, the new MaineCare Partner Portal is scheduled to go live on October 12, 2026, at 8:00 AM. The new portal will replace the current HealthPAS Online Portal and will require Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA). Read below for more information and steps you will need to take to sign into the MaineCare Partner Portal starting on October 12. 

For all information about the upcoming changes to MIHMS, see the “HealthPAS Online Portal” section of the Provider Resources page.  

Multi-Factor Authenticator (MFA) 

MFA adds a second verification step after entering your password. This is an important new security measure to protect the sensitive information held in the Portal. You will have three options to choose from for your additional authentication factor; you must choose one.

Follow the instructions below for first-time setup of the option you choose. 

  1. Microsoft Authenticator 

The Microsoft Authenticator app is the recommended MFA method because it offers the highest level of protection over other methods. Download the Microsoft Authenticator app now on a smartphone or tablet so that you are ready to use it on October 12. 

No sooner than October 12, follow these steps to set up MFA via the app:  

Trading Partners with existing (migrated) Portal accounts: 

  • Open the Microsoft Authenticator app. 
  • Click “Sign In” on the MaineCare Partner Portal; you will see a User Details window pop up. 
  • Click the QR code scanner in the Microsoft Authenticator app and scan the QR code displayed on the Portal’s User Details window.  

Trading Partners without existing (new or non-migrated) Portal accounts will set this up as part of the registration process.

 

  1. Text/Call 

Text (SMS) or call verification is available as an MFA option through September 2027.  

No sooner than October 12, follow these steps to set up MFA via text (SMS) or call: 

Trading Partners with existing (migrated) Portal accounts: 

  • Click “Sign In” on the MaineCare Partner Portal; you will see a User Details window pop up. 
  • Select the “Text/call” option then click “Continue.” 
  • Enter a phone number, request a code or call, then verify the code. The phone number you provide during setup will be saved as your registered MFA contact method and will be used for future authentication and account verification activities. 

Trading Partners without existing (new or non-migrated) Portal accounts will set this up as part of the registration process.

 

  1. Email 

Email verification is available as an MFA option through September 2027. 

No sooner than October 12, follow these steps to set up MFA via email: 

Trading Partners with existing (migrated) Portal accounts: 

  • Click “Sign In” on the MaineCare Partner Portal; you will see a User Details window pop up. 
  • Select the “Email” option then click “Continue.” 
  • Enter an email address, request a code, then verify the code. The email address you provide during setup will be saved as your registered MFA contact method and will be used for future authentication and account verification activities. 

Trading Partners without existing (new or non-migrated) Portal accounts will set this up as part of the registration process. 

 

For additional instructions on both initial setup and ongoing use of MFA, including screenshots, please reference the job aid MaineCare Partner Portal MFA Setup and Access Job Aid. 

  • You can find this job aid and other supporting resources through the MMIS Learning Center. Search for the course “ME – MIHMS Upgrade Documentation,” enroll in the course, then look for the job aid in the documentation list. 
  • Starting October 12, 2026, this job aid will also be available in the MaineCare Partner Portal under the Provider tab > Provider Manuals subtab. 

Need Help? 

If you have questions about these instructions, please call Provider Services at 1-866-690-5585. 

Thank you for preparing in advance for a smooth transition to the new MaineCare Partner Portal.

"The State Workforce Development Board plays a critical role in coordinating Maine's workforce development efforts to support economic growth and address workforce challenges," said Maine Department of Labor Commissioner Laura Fortman. "Vaughan Woodruff is a well-respected business leader with deep workforce expertise. His continued leadership will help maintain momentum as we strengthen Maine's workforce and economy."

"I appreciate the trust that Gov. Mills and the Maine Senate have placed in me through my nomination and confirmation to continue serving the people of Maine in this role," said Woodruff. "I feel privileged to work with the outstanding staff and members of the Board to increase the accessibility of the workforce system to Maine workers and businesses and to proactively address the workforce challenges ahead of us."

Woodruff is a seventh-generation Maine native who was raised in Pittsfield. He earned a bachelor's degree in civil engineering from the University of Maine and a master's degree in education from Prescott College in Arizona. Woodruff was the founder and CEO of Insource Renewables, an employee-owned solar company that was recognized as a Best for the World for Workers company by B Lab prior to its acquisition by ReVision Energy in 2021.

During Woodruff's tenure as chair, the SWDB has:

  • Launched Work Source Maine, the state's online resource connecting job seekers, students, parents, educators, career counselors and employers with resources to explore, plan and achieve career and workforce goals;

  • Launched the Maine Workforce Pell program, which expands federal Pell Grant eligibility to approved short-term, career-focused training programs that deliver industry-recognized credentials and measurable employment results, preparing students for in-demand occupations; and

  • Secured $15M+ in funding to support industry partnerships in advanced manufacturing, forest bioproducts and defense, and expand career exploration, job supports, and upskilling investments including registered pre-apprenticeships

As chair, Woodruff will continue to work with the SWDB, state agencies, education and training providers, employers and other partners to strengthen Maine's workforce development system and help connect Maine people with career opportunities.

Woodruff serves on the Electrical Technologies Advisory Committee at Kennebec Valley Community College and previously served on the Western Mountains Committee of the Maine Community Foundation and the Pittsfield Planning Board. Woodruff lives in Pittsfield with his wife, Holly Zadra, and their two sons, Eamon and Goran.

This poster explaining how to mark the ranked-choice ballot (PDF) is posted in every voting booth on Election Day.

Fact Sheet:

This PDF provides the facts voters need to know about voting in a ranked-choice election.

What is the process for tabulating ranked-choice ballots? (PDF)

Ranked choice voting results tabulation glossary

This glossary explains the terms used in the ranked-choice voting results grid that is produced to explain the results of any ranked-choice race. See our Election Results page.

Round 1

This is the first round of ranked-choice voting tabulation, which begins to apply the RCV rules onto the ballots that were cast on Election Day. (Note: The unofficial Election Day tally can be considered as Round 0). For example, if a voter did not mark any candidate as their first choice, their ballot was counted as blank on election night. In Round 1, if the voter marked the ballot for their second choice candidate, their vote is bumped up and counted, per the RCV rules.) Rounds continue until only two candidates remain and the winner is determined as the candidate with more than 50% of the votes in that final round.

Exhausted ballot

There are no valid votes in any ranking on the voter’s ballot for any continuing candidate (a candidate who is still in the race and has not been defeated). Types of exhausted ballots:

  • Exhausted choices: For those ballots that are exhausted by exhausted choices, all of the voter’s candidate choices have been eliminated from the race. (Note: If they cast a vote for a candidate who has been eliminated, their vote remains with that candidate, just as it would in a plurality race if they had voted for the losing candidate.)
  • Undervote: The voter did not mark any candidates, or refrained from ranking, in that choice category (1st, 2nd, 3rd). Those whose ballots are exhausted by undervote either didn’t vote in this race at all, or they left BOTH their first and second choices blank (in which case, we do not look any further down their ballot, per the RCV rules).
  • Overvote: The voter chose more than one candidate for that ranking. For example, the voter marked BOTH Candidate A and Candidate B as their choice.

Continuing ballots

All ballots that include a valid vote for a continuing candidate, and therefore have not been exhausted.

Transfer

The votes that go to a continuing candidate when another candidate is eliminated. This is determined by reviewing each ballot initially cast for the eliminated candidate. The elections software looks further down each voter’s ballot to see if the voter ranked another candidate who is still in the race, and if so, it moves or “transfers” their vote to that candidate (For example: Your vote transfers to your second choice candidate if your first choice candidate is eliminated from the race).

Total=

Ballot Exhausted by Overvotes + Ballot Exhausted by Undervotes + Exhausted Ballot + Continuing Ballots.

Board of Occupational Safety and Health to Host Listening Sessions on Proposed Indoor Air Quality Compliance Directive

October 6, 2026

For Immediate Release

Media Contact: Autumn Mahoney, Communications Specialist media.dol@maine.gov

AUGUSTA - The Board of Occupational Safety and Health (BOSH) and the Maine Department of Labor Bureau of Labor Standards (BLS) Workplace Safety and Health Division invite interested parties and the public to participate in listening sessions on a proposed voluntary compliance directive on indoor air quality.

BOSH regulates and enforces workplace safety and health rules that apply to public employers, including state and local governmental agencies, school districts and quasi-governmental agencies. BOSH is considering publishing a voluntary compliance directive to help public employers monitor and maintain healthy indoor air quality in public workplaces. The proposed compliance directive is based in part on the research and recommendations of the Indoor Air Quality Advisory Group in 2025.

item.title: US Department of Labor cites Pennsylvania excavation employer for failing to provide trench protection following fatal trench cave-in — U.S. Department of Labor — News Releases
item.description: CHAMBERSBURG, PA – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited an excavation contractor for willful and serious safety violations after a young worker was fatally injured in a trench collapse. The department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration opened an investigation into Jonas David Wagoner – doing business as J.D. Wagoner Excavating – on April 2, 2026, and found workers were installing a storm sewer system 12 feet below ground level in a trench that was not adequately protected from soil collapse. When a portion of the trench's wall failed, the unrestrained soil engulfed one worker. The agency issued a willful violation for failure to protect workers from cave-ins and two repeat violations for failing to assign a competent person to conduct daily trench inspections and removing employees from hazardous conditions.In addition, the employer received three serious violations for failure to provide construction hazard prevention training to employees, establish a safe means for workers to exit the excavation site, keep materials at least two feet from the edge of an excavation site, and restrain side materials from becoming roll-in hazards. OSHA proposed $254,884 in penalties. The employer has 15 business days from receiving receipt of its citations and penalties to request an informal conference with OSHA’s area director or contest the findings before the independent Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission. Please check the OSHA establishment search page periodically for any changes in the inspection or penalty status.Visit OSHA’s website to learn about keeping workers safe around trenching and excavations. Employers can also contact the agency for information about OSHA’s compliance assistance resources and for free help on complying with OSHA standards.

PANEL MEMBERS: Administrative Law Judges Biddings, Chabot, and Rooks By: Administrative Law Judge Biddings [¶1] Jerome Weiss appeals from a decision of a Workers’ Compensation Board administrative law judge ( Smith, ALJ) denying his Petition to Reopen for Mistake of Fact or Fraud. Mr. Weiss contends that the ALJ erred in determining that his petition was untimely under 39-A M.R.S.A. § 321(2), and in concluding that even if the petition had been timely, Mr. Weiss did not establish that Maine Soapstone Company committed fraud. We disagree with Mr. Weiss’s contentions and affirm the decision.
2
I. BACKGROUND1 [¶2] Mr. Weiss sustained a work-related shoulder injury on February 3, 2009, while working for Maine Soapstone Company. Initially, Maine Soapstone voluntarily paid Mr. Weiss lost time and medical benefits. On September 13, 2010, Maine Soapstone issued a 21-day letter informing Mr. Weiss and the board of their intention to discontinue Mr. Weiss’s benefits as of October 5, 2010. See 39-A M.R.S.A. § 205(9). [¶3] In response to the discontinuance of his benefits, Mr. Weiss filed a Petition for Review , Request for Provisional Order , and a Petition for Award of Compensation regarding the February 3, 2009, date of injury. During the litigation, Mr. Weiss underwent an independent medical examination with Dr. Hall. See 39-A M.R.S.A. § 312. Dr. Hall opined that the effects of Mr. Weiss’s injury were ongoing and that he had retained a partial work capacity. An evidentiary hearing was held on May 16, 2011, before a board hearing officer (Pelletier, HO).2

MaineCare in Education: Updated Joint Individual Education Program (IEP) Guidance for School Health-Related Services

Oct 08, 2026

As a reminder, all providers who deliver services following the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) must ensure all MaineCare-covered services are documented following the Department of Health and Human Services/Maine Department of Education Joint IEP Guidance document. 

The Maine Department of Education has released updated Joint IEP Guidance to help schools follow federal and state requirements. The updated guidance was developed through a collaborative effort and is available on the MaineCare in Education web page. 

DOE first released the Joint Guidance on August 28, 2026, and has re-issued this guidance effective September 18, 2026. The reissued guidance replaces the previously issued Joint Guidance and provides clarification in response to questions and feedback received from School Administrative Units (SAUs), providers, and other interested parties. 

All IEP documents must reflect the updated guidance as soon as possible, but no later than thirty (30) days of the issuance of the guidance. 

Providers with current prior authorizations for School Health-Related Services through Acentra should upload any updated documentation to Atrezzo. Acentra will accept IEP language from both versions through October 18, 2026. Beginning October 19, 2026, Acentra will only accept IEP language from the new version re-issued on September 18, 2026. 

For technical assistance regarding the billing and processing of MaineCare claims, please contact your Provider Relations Specialist. 

For all other questions related to the provision of MaineCare School Health-Related Services, please contact Trista Collins, State Medicaid Educational Liaison.    

For technical information related to IEP development, please contact Dan Hemdal at the Maine Department of Education.

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Contact: Danna Hayes

Danna.hayes@maine.gov

If You Bought Certain Generic Prescription Drugs in the United States Between May 2009 and December 2019, You Could be Eligible for Money

AUGUSTA – Attorney General Aaron M. Frey today joined a coalition of 45 states and territories seeking court approval of three settlements with Ascend Laboratories, Citron Pharma and Mayne Pharma to resolve allegations that the generic drug manufacturers engaged in a widespread, long-running conspiracy to artificially inflate and manipulate prices, reduce competition, and unreasonably restrain trade with regard to numerous generic prescription drugs.

Ascend will pay $400,000 to the states. Mayne will pay $650,000. Citron’s settlement only includes non-monetary terms as it has ceased business operations. As part of the settlement, the companies each agreed to meaningful injunctive terms including a series of internal reforms to ensure fair competition and compliance with antitrust laws. 

These latest settlements come as the States prepare for the first trial to be held in Hartford, Connecticut in February 2027.  

The States previously reached settlements with Sandoz, Glenmark, Lannett, Bausch, Apotex, Heritage, and Heritage’s parent company, Emcure, totaling $496.5 million.

If you purchased a generic prescription drug between May 2009 and December 2019, you may be eligible for compensation. To determine your eligibility, call 1-866-290-0182 (Toll-Free), email info@AGGenericDrugs.com or visit www.AGGenericDrugs.com. You can submit a claim for compensation.

Connecticut is leading a coalition of nearly all states and territories engaged in a series of antitrust cases, starting first in 2016. The first Complaint included Heritage and 17 other corporate Defendants, two individual Defendants, and 15 generic drugs. Two former executives from Heritage Pharmaceuticals, Jeffery Glazer and Jason Malek, have since entered into settlement agreements and are cooperating. The second Complaint was filed in 2019 against Teva Pharmaceuticals and 21 of the nation’s largest generic drug manufacturers. The Complaint names 16 individual senior executive Defendants. The third complaint, to be tried first, focuses on 80 topical generic drugs that account for billions of dollars of sales in the United States and names 26 corporate defendants and 10 individual defendants. The States filed a fourth complaint earlier this year, alleging that Novartis AG, Sandoz Group AG and Sandoz AG, are liable for Sandoz’s alleged conduct and for fraudulently transferring assets.

The cases all stem from a series of investigations built on evidence from several cooperating witnesses at the core of the different conspiracies, a massive document database of more than 20 million documents, and a phone records database containing millions of call detail records and contact information for more than 600 sales and pricing individuals in the generics industry. Each complaint addresses a different set of drugs and defendants and lays out an interconnected web of competing industry executives that met with each other during industry dinners, "girls’ nights out," lunches, cocktail parties, golf outings, and communicated via frequent telephone calls, emails, and text messages that sowed the seeds for their illegal agreements. Throughout the complaints, defendants use terms like "fair share," "playing nice in the sandbox," and "responsible competitor" to describe how they unlawfully discouraged competition, raised prices, and enforced an ingrained culture of collusion. Among the records obtained by the States is a two-volume notebook containing the contemporaneous notes of one of the States’ cooperators that memorialized his discussions during phone calls with competitors and internal company meetings over a period of several years.

States and territories also joining the settlements include: Alaska, Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, the District of Columbia, Florida, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Montana, Nebraska, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Puerto Rico, Rhode Island, South Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, Washington, West Virginia, Wisconsin, and Wyoming.
